next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST (FIN7): a financially driven group that moved from card theft toward ransomware
next.in_short: Researchers describe GOLD LOCUST, better known as FIN7, as a financially motivated group with origins in Russia. It has used phishing, USB mailings and custom tools, and from 2020 it moved toward ransomware, according to SentinelOne.

sentences.t: The catalogue record for GOLD LOCUST lists the aliases Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider and FIN7.
SentinelOne describes FIN7 as an elusive, persistent and financially motivated threat group with origins in Russia.

SentinelOne says that from 2020 the group shifted its focus to ransomware and affiliated with RaaS groups such as REvil and Conti. It also says the group launched its own RaaS programmes, Darkside and then BlackMatter.
S2W also reports that Darkside, known to be used by FIN7, was rebranded to BlackMatter.
SentinelOne says the group caused substantial financial losses in industries such as hospitality, energy, finance, high-tech and retail.
FireEye wrote in 2017 that FIN7 kept hitting the restaurant, hospitality and financial services sectors.
BleepingComputer reports that in 2018 the group hacked Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord & Taylor to steal payment card information.
The FBI said FIN7 mailed packages through USPS to retail, restaurant and hotel businesses.

In the FBI's account, the mailed USB drives were set up to type keystrokes. The report says they launched PowerShell commands that fetched GRIFFON malware. One package posed as a Best Buy gift-card offer.
Malwarebytes attributes a late-June 2022 malspam campaign to FIN7. It dropped JSSLoader, which Malwarebytes describes as a rewrite with added data exfiltration, and a second .NET payload.
Morphisec described a chain that began with a phishing invoice lure. VBScript stages ran in memory, and a script then loaded Carbanak reflectively.

SentinelOne says FIN7 has historically used Carbanak, a privately developed backdoor. NCC Group, as reported by The Hacker News, saw Carbanak in ransomware attacks. Compromised websites hosted installers posing as business software such as HubSpot, Veeam and Xero.
SentinelOne assesses with high confidence that several forum sellers of AV-killer tools belong to the FIN7 cluster. Its AvNeutralizer tool uses a driver-based method to tamper with security products.
SentinelOne attributes automated SQL injection intrusions, run through a platform called Checkmarks, to FIN7 with medium confidence.
Harfanglab analysed PackXOR, a packer that Sentinel Labs linked to AvNeutralizer. Harfanglab says the packer appears to be used for activity unrelated to FIN7, including by ransomware operators.
SentinelLABS reported in November 2022 that Black Basta ransomware attacks deployed custom EDR evasion tools it ties to FIN7.

Rapid7 cites GData attributing a Python RAT to FIN7. Rapid7 also assesses that the developers of a Java malware family are likely initial access brokers who may have provided access to Black Basta and/or FIN7 affiliates.
SentinelOne says it cannot conclusively determine whether LockBit intrusions involving AvNeutralizer were carried out by FIN7. It says no direct evidence links them to the group.
Treat unexpected USB drives, invoice attachments and software installers from unfamiliar sites as untrusted.
Keep security tools protected against tampering, and review access to remote administration tools.
